title: Two-Step Equations
short: Undo adding or subtracting, then undo multiplying or dividing.
trouble: Students divide before undoing the addition, and then divide only part of the equation.

blocks.html: In $3x + 5 = 20$, two things happened to $x$: it was multiplied by 3, and then 5 was added. You know how to undo each one from one-step equations. The question is the order.
Undo the steps in reverse order: first undo the adding or subtracting, then undo the multiplying or dividing. Do each step to the whole of both sides.

Getting dressed, you put on socks, then shoes. Undressing, you take off the shoes first. Here $x$ was multiplied first and the 5 was added last, so the 5 comes off first. You could divide first, but then every term must be divided, $x + \frac{5}{3} = \frac{20}{3}$, which is correct but messier.

blocks.name: balance
blocks.cap: Take 5 cubes off both sides, then split what is left into 3 equal parts.

blocks.name: tapediagram
blocks.cap: The same equation as a tape: three equal boxes and 5 more make 20. Press "Next step".

blocks.html: Dividing only part of a side: from $3x + 5 = 20$ writing $x + 5 = \frac{20}{3}$. If you divide, you must divide every term. Safer: undo the $+5$ first. Always check by substituting your answer into the original equation.
